findings.title: registerIDPLoginInvalidation called with possibly null idp without null check
findings.body: In remove(), storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) may be null if the IDP doesn't exist (alias not found). registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp) then calls getLoginPredicate().test(idp) which internally checks Objects::nonNull first, so it won't NPE, but it silently returns false and skips invalidation — fine functionally. However, registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp) at line 103 (in the isInvalid branch) will NPE if storedIdp is null since it directly calls idp.getInternalId() without a null check, unlike before this change there was no such path change but it still exists as a latent bug exposed via removed/invalid aliases.

findings.title: getForLogin cache does not account for 'mode' granularity across ORG_ONLY organizationId variations consistently with getByOrganization caching
findings.body: The IdentityProviderListQuery cache for getForLogin keys on cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode) and the per-organizationId filter result is stored as a sub key, similar to getByOrganization. However, when mode=ORG_ONLY and organizationId is null (fetch all org-linked IDPs), searchKey becomes empty string "", colliding conceptually with REALM_ONLY's empty search key semantics on a different cache key — this is probably fine since cacheKeyForLogin includes mode, but there's no invalidation differentiation per organization: any organization-level IDP change invalidates ALL cached searchKeys for all organizations under ORG_ONLY/ALL modes (via registerIDPLoginInvalidation iterating over all FetchMode and clearing the whole cacheKey), which means caching granularity per organizationId provides no benefit since the entire list query entry is invalidated together, causing cache thrashing for multi-tenant setups with frequent IDP updates in different orgs.

findings.title: getLoginPredicate behavior change may have broader than intended effect
findings.body: getLoginPredicate() now adds an extra condition requiring BROKER_PUBLIC=true for any idp with an organizationId, applied in both getForLogin's default implementation context and the invalidation logic in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider. This predicate is reused for cache invalidation decisions (create/remove/update) but the default getForLogin implementation uses separate search options (not getLoginPredicate directly) for building search criteria, so there's a risk of divergence between the actual query logic (search options) and the invalidation logic (predicate) if the two implementations are not kept in sync, since they must independently encode the same business rules (enabled, not link-only, not hidden, org public check) in two separate places.
